critical_interface_constraints: Finite triangulation of a noncompact space means |K| minus a subcomplex |D| in a compactification, not |K| itself.
Compatible stratifications for maps mean smooth stratumwise submersions; properness is on the whole map, not on each restriction to a nonclosed stratum.
No assertion that arbitrary projective algebraic maps become simplicial.
Real simplicial strata supply real-dimensional conical products, not smooth complex algebraic strata.
Internal derived Hom of constructible sheaves needs actual derived sheaf/diagram comparison and controlled transport; topology or cohomology-sheaf local constancy alone is not the proof.

For all separated finite-type complex varieties beyond quasi-projective KLR spaces, require semialgebraic realization/gluing or a proper compactification supplier; no unjustified global projective embedding.
